title: Will New York Raise Taxes on the Rich? Free Child Care May Depend on It.
summary: With Gov. Kathy Hochul and Mayor Zohran Mamdani pushing to expand free child care, a tax-the-rich campaign may fare better next year in a more left-leaning environment.

There are few ideas in New York politics as simultaneously galvanizing and polarizing as that of raising taxes on the rich — not to keep the city running, but to pay for a vast expansion of the social safety network.


The[perennial policy long shot](https://www.nytimes.com/2014/01/22/nyregion/cuomo-prekindergarten-proposal.html) now has momentum on its side.


Mayor Zohran Mamdani, a democratic socialist who was catapulted into office on a pledge to tax the rich, and Gov. Kathy Hochul, a business-friendly moderate[fresh off an electoral romp](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/08/nyregion/kathy-hochul-2028-ny.html) , have both committed to expanding free child care.


Offering free, government-subsidized child care to all New York City children under 5, as the mayor[has promised to do](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/31/nyregion/mamdani-child-care-upper-east-side.html) , could cost[$9 billion](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/03/nyregion/mamdani-free-child-care-cost.html) or even up to[$12 billion](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/64989b0dc1b2fa02e6188180/t/673c98333262f44fce460451/1732024373382/NYUC+UPC+Full+Report.pdf) a year, according to recent estimates, much more than the city currently spends on child care.


Finding that money each year leads to the trickier question of whether the wealthiest people in New York City, the global center of capitalism, should foot the bill.


When asked about raising taxes in recent weeks, Ms. Hochul has pointed to the state’s strong fiscal position — it has about $8 billion more in tax revenues than expected — but also left the door open to some form of a tax increase, which would require her support.


The governor has blanched at what she sees as the reflexive desire of some Democrats to tax the rich, particularly because New York already has some of the highest taxes in the country. But she is prepared to raise certain taxes, and tie those increases directly to child care, two people familiar with the matter said. How much the increases could be and who might be affected are not yet clear.
